what: Morrow, a young acolyte of a death cult disguised as a priest, painted seriously: a thin, wiry man of about twenty-five with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight heads tall. His face is sly and untrustworthy, a con-man's face: a wide crooked sneering grin showing his teeth, narrowed knowing eyes slid sideways, one eyebrow cocked high, a sharp nose, a stubbled chin, weather-beaten light tan skin. His short dark hair is cropped close to his skull. He is a living man.
colours: a plain black wool cassock with dark charcoal-grey highlights on the folds, a white linen band collar at the throat, weather-beaten light tan face and hands, dark hair, a short knife of bright pale steel.
wears: He wears a stolen priest's robe: one plain black cassock buttoned from the throat to the ankles with a row of small black buttons, a narrow white linen collar band at his throat, sleeves a little too long for him, a plain black cord belt, and scuffed black leather shoes. He has no hood, a bare head, no armour, no jewellery and no cross.
holds: He holds exactly one short knife no longer than his hand, of bright pale steel with a small black wooden handle, in his left hand, held low and back beside his left thigh with the blade pointing down, half hidden in the folds of the cassock. His right hand is raised high beside his head with two fingers held up in a priest's blessing, a bare hand, nothing in it or near it.
pose: On two legs, seen a little from the side, he creeps forward to the right in a long sly stride, hunched and leaning forward, his front knee bent and his back heel lifted, his shoulders hunched, his right hand raised high in a false blessing, his left hand trailing the knife low behind his thigh, his head turned back over his shoulder toward the viewer with a sneering grin.
must_show: a thin young man in a plain black buttoned cassock with a white collar band
a sly face: narrowed sideways eyes, crooked smile
one short knife held low behind his hip
the other hand raised in a blessing, empty
bare head, cropped dark hair

what: a herald of the Cult of the Locust, a lightly armed messenger who carries the cult's orders down the deep roads, painted seriously: a lean, quick living man of about thirty with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight heads tall. His face is clever and smooth-talking: a thin trimmed black moustache, a pointed chin, watchful dark eyes, weather-beaten light tan skin, black hair tied back. He is dressed for the road, not for battle.
colours: a long travel cloak of dull ash-grey wool, a dark charcoal-grey tunic, a dark scuffed chestnut-brown leather satchel and belt, cream parchment scrolls, a short knife of pale steel, dark brown boots, and one small badge of dull brass on his chest.
wears: He wears a long ash-grey wool travel cloak thrown back over his shoulders and pinned at the throat, a knee-length dark charcoal-grey tunic, a broad dark brown leather belt, dark brown riding boots, and on the left of his chest one brass badge as big as his palm in the shape of a locust seen from above. Across his body on a strap hangs one old courier's satchel of dark scuffed chestnut-brown leather, worn at his right hip, its flap thrown open, with three fat rolled cream parchment scrolls standing up out of it, each as thick as his thumb and sticking up a hand's length above the satchel, plain to see. He has no helmet, no mask, a bare head, no armour and no shield.
holds: He holds exactly two things: in his left hand one rolled cream parchment scroll with a dangling black wax seal, held up beside his face as if reading out an order; in his right hand one short knife no longer than his hand, of pale steel, held low at his side, point forward.
pose: On two legs, he strides to the left in mid-step, his body turned three quarters to the viewer, the scroll held up high beside his face in his left hand, the short knife low in his right, the travel cloak swinging out behind him, his mouth open as if proclaiming.
must_show: a lean living man in a long ash-grey travel cloak, bare head
a leather satchel with scroll ends sticking out
one scroll held up in one hand
one short knife in the other hand
lightly dressed: no helmet, no shield, no mask, no armour

what: a soldier of the Cult of the Locust, who hold the last roads down to the Pit, painted seriously: a tall, broad, living human warrior of the dark ages with realistic adult proportions, two arms and two legs, about eight heads tall, whose whole head is hidden inside an old forged helmet made in the shape of a giant locust's head. The helmet is blackened iron, dark gunmetal grey: its face is a long blunt grasshopper's face that slopes down and forward to a squared-off jaw below his chin, with jointed plates along it like the plates of an insect's face and two short curved iron mandibles like small hooked tusks at its bottom corners; on each side of the helmet one huge smooth dome of dull yellow glass is set flush into the iron like the compound eye of an insect, each a third of the helmet wide, with no rim, no strap and no lens frame; from the top of the brow two long thick curved iron feelers, each as thick as a finger, sweep back over the helmet. It reads at once as an insect's head, but it is a helmet worn by a man: his neck and shoulders are a man's.
colours: a blackened iron locust helmet, dark gunmetal grey, with two huge dull yellow glass eye-lenses; dark blackened iron mail; long ragged robes of dull ash-grey with darker soot-grey shadows covering his chest and body; a plain black shield with a pale grey worn rim; a dark wooden spear shaft with a pale steel head.
wears: He wears no plate armour. His chest, belly and shoulders are covered by long ragged robes of dull ash-grey cloth, a hooded mantle thrown back off the helmet, belted at the waist with a broad black leather belt, the robe falling in torn strips to his shins. Under the robes a mail shirt of blackened iron, dark gunmetal grey, shows only on his arms to the wrists; dark leather gloves, black boots.
holds: He holds exactly two things: on his left arm one tall plain black shield, the only shield in the picture, an upright oval as tall as from his chin to his knee, plain black all over with a dented pale grey iron rim and nothing painted on it; in his right hand one tall spear held upright beside him like a sentry: a long straight dark wooden shaft, perfectly straight, as straight as a ruler, standing straight up and down, its one broad leaf-shaped pale steel head high above his helmet at the top of the picture, its lower end plain bare wood beside his right foot with nothing on it.
pose: On two legs, he stands guard at a checkpoint in a wide braced stance, his weight on his front leg and his body turned three quarters to the viewer, the black shield held up across his body on his left arm, the upright spear gripped in his right fist at shoulder height, its head high above him, his locust-helmed head lowered and thrust forward toward the viewer.
must_show: a man in a blackened iron helmet shaped like a locust's head, two big yellow insect eyes, two swept-back feelers
exactly one tall plain black shield
one upright spear with one head at the top
ash-grey ragged robes over dark mail
a human body: two arms, two legs

what: Neferkaptah risen: the drowned undead prince of ancient Egypt, a mummy-sorcerer come up out of the Nile, painted seriously, plainly a lord and far grander than a common mummy. He is a tall, gaunt, long-limbed corpse with realistic adult proportions, a small head, about eight heads tall, never stout. From the top of his head to the soles of his feet he is completely wound in linen bandages, layer over layer, like a figure built out of bandage, and no skin shows anywhere: his chest, his belly, both arms to the fingertips, each hand like a bandaged mitten with long wrapped fingers, his legs and his feet are all wrapped, the bands running slantwise and crossing. His head is a rounded bundle of bandages wound round and round, crossing over the top of the head, over the forehead, the nose, the cheeks, the mouth and the chin, so that the head has no face at all, only wrappings; in one dark gap between two bands, where the eyes would be, glow two round eyes of solid bright pale blue light, each as big as a thumbnail, the brightest things in the picture. Every bandage is soaked dark with river water: dark wet grey-brown, the colour of mud at the bottom of a river, shining wet on the ridges, with dark lines between the bands, and drops of water hang from his fingertips. Round his neck and over his shoulders lies a broad Egyptian collar of gold: a wide half-moon of gold beads in five rows, from his throat out to the points of his shoulders, bright and heavy over the dark wet wrappings. Across his chest, from one shoulder to the opposite hip, a single broad band of pale linen is tied tight, the knot of the band on his shoulder. On his head, round the wrapped skull, is a thin gold circlet with a small gold cobra rearing at the front of it.
colours: dark wet grey-brown bandages on every part of him, head, face, chest, arms, hands, legs and feet, shining wet on the ridges, dark brown lines between the bands; a broad bright gold bead collar in five rows; a thin gold circlet with a gold cobra; a pale undyed linen band across his chest; a dark brown leather-bound book; two solid bright pale blue glowing eyes.
wears: He wears nothing but his wet bandages, the broad gold collar, the gold circlet with its cobra, a gold band round each upper arm, and the pale linen band tied across his chest holding the book-box. He has no kilt, no robe and no cloak.
holds: He holds exactly one thing: in his right wrapped hand, pressed flat against his chest under the linen band, one thick old book bound in dark brown leather. His left wrapped arm is stretched out ahead of him, the bandaged fingers spread and clawing, reaching to seize; the left hand is empty, with no light, no flame and no magic in it. He holds no staff.
pose: On two legs, he lurches forward to the left in a stiff, heavy stride, dragging his back foot, his left arm stretched out ahead with the dead fingers clawing, his right hand pressing the book to his chest, his head thrust forward with the two blue-white eyes glaring at the viewer.
must_show: a tall gaunt figure wound in dark, wet, grey-brown bandages from head to foot, arms and hands included, no skin anywhere
the head a bundle of bandages with no face, two glowing pale blue eyes
a broad bright gold bead collar over the shoulders
a pale linen band across his chest; one book held to his chest
gold circlet; plainly grander than a plain mummy
one hand reaching, empty, no magic, no staff

what: Azarael, a fallen angel of the Powers, the third rank of angels, newly broken out of his chains, painted seriously as a terrible fallen angel and not as a horned devil. He is immense, lean and wiry, fully fleshed, with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight heads tall. He is not a man of flesh and no part of him is the colour of skin: his whole body, his face, his head, his arms, his hands and his feet, is cast bronze like an ancient statue come alive, dark bronze, the colour of an old bronze statue, deep brown-gold, nearly black in the hollows, and it is split all over by a net of wide, deep, jagged cracks like the cracks in cooling lava, each crack as wide as a finger, in which fire glows bright yellow-gold and white-hot from inside, like the bars of a furnace door; about a dozen big cracks run across his chest and belly, down both arms to the wrists and down both thighs, so that a quarter of his body is glowing light and he plainly burns from within. His bronze is darker than gold, a deep brown bronze, so that the glowing cracks stand out bright against it. His head is a bronze statue's head: a stern, beautiful, terrible angel's face of bronze with a straight nose and a hard mouth, its curling hair cast in the same dark bronze, and eyes that are two spots of solid white-gold light. He has no horns. From his shoulder blades rise two great wings of ragged coal-black feathers, black as soot, torn and broken, bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, tips pointing down, the feathers singed grey at their edges.
colours: dark cast bronze on every part of him, deep brown-gold, nearly black in the hollows, split by wide cracks glowing bright yellow-gold and white-hot; two solid white-gold eyes; ragged coal-black feathered wings singed grey at the tips; blackened iron manacles and heavy gunmetal grey chain links; a scorched charcoal-grey robe.
wears: He wears a long ragged robe of scorched charcoal-grey cloth, its hem burnt and torn, belted with a band of blackened iron, the robe covering him from waist to shins and thrown over his left shoulder, so that only his right shoulder, his arms and part of his chest show the cracked glowing bronze. On each wrist is one heavy blackened iron manacle, a thick cuff as wide as his hand, and from each manacle hangs a short length of broken chain: three big oval links, each link as big as his fist, gunmetal grey, the last link snapped open, plain against the backdrop.
holds: His hands are empty: two great bronze fists, clenched, glowing gold at the knuckles. He holds nothing.
pose: He is rising from a kneel: his right foot is planted forward with the right knee bent up high, his left knee is bent down low with the left lower leg tucked back behind him, the left knee floating just above where a floor would be. His body is surging upward and forward, both fists raised in front of his chest at different heights with the broken chains swinging from the manacles, his wings arched up behind him, his head lifted and his white-gold eyes blazing at the viewer.
must_show: a huge figure of dark cast bronze with wide cracks glowing yellow-gold like a furnace from within: not skin
a stern angel's bronze face, no horns, two white-gold eyes
two ragged soot-black feathered wings
an iron manacle on each wrist with big broken chain links hanging
fists raised, empty hands
